content: 1. A study published in BMC Public Health in June 2021 investigated the prevalence of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection among the general population in the Nile Delta region of Egypt. The study is accessible via DOI: 10.1186/s12889-021-11169-x, with the PubMed ID (PMID) 34158006 and PubMed Central ID (PMCID) PMC8218412. 2. Majam M, Fischer A, Ivanova Reipold E, Rhagnath N, Msolomba V, and Lalla-Edward ST conducted a study assessing the usability and interpretation of a hepatitis C virus self-testing device by lay users in Johannesburg, South Africa. This research was published in Diagnostics (Basel) in March 2021, volume 11, issue 3, article 463. The DOI is 10.3390/diagnostics11030463, with PMID 33800060 and PMCID PMC8000311. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) published a report in 2021 addressing global health priorities and strategies. This publication provides critical insights into public health initiatives and guidelines. 4. Oru E, Trickey A, Shirali R, Kanters S, and Easterbrook P conducted a global systematic review and meta-analysis on decentralization, integration, and task-shifting in hepatitis C virus testing and treatment. Their findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in April 2021, volume 9, issue 4, pages e431–e445. 5. Castro R, Perazzo H, de Araujo LAMM, Gutierres IG, Grinsztejn B, and Veloso VG evaluated the effectiveness of implementing decentralized delivery of hepatitis C virus treatment using direct-acting antivirals. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in PLOS One in February 2020, article e0229143. The study was made available on February 21, 2020. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) released consolidated guidelines in 2016 on HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care for key populations. These guidelines are available online at the WHO website under the publication reference 9789241511124. 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) also published the Global Health Sector Strategy on Viral Hepatitis 2016–2021 in June 2016. This document outlines strategic approaches to combat viral hepatitis on a global scale.
